A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MonoSoup work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched reliably across reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MonoSoup evaluations on CLIP, Qwen, and ConvNeXt, together with spectral ablations and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds multilingual and cross-domain evaluations, a LoRA experiment, computational profiling, and Model Stock failure cases.

M1.justification: The SVD decomposition, fixed-threshold and effective-rank partitions, and spectral weighting equations remain unchanged, as does Similarity-Filtered Greedy Soup. The LoRA experiment applies the existing MonoSoup procedure after merging adapters into model weights.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds MGSM evaluation across eight languages and cross-domain tests on ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, and MMLU humanities/social sciences after English mathematics fine-tuning. These substantially extend v1's language coverage. ConvNeXt was already evaluated; its changed pretraining label and unchanged checkpoint link do not establish an actual coverage change.

E2.justification: Table 8 introduces an unedited LoRA/RSLoRA-fine-tuned checkpoint as the comparator for LoRA plus MonoSoup. Existing Model Soups, Model Stock, LiNeS, and Wise-FT comparisons remain. LoRA-Pro and PiSSA are discussed but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce eight-shot native chain-of-thought MGSM evaluation, zero-shot cross-domain evaluation, an English-only MetaMathQA checkpoint, and rank-8 LoRA training on 100,000 samples for one epoch. Computational profiling adds four model scales through Qwen3-14B on an A100. These are additional protocols, not demonstrated reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of cross-lingual and cross-domain robustness, compatibility with low-rank adaptation, computational scaling, and extreme Model Stock failures. Existing CKA, truncation, threshold, and anisotropic-scaling analyses are retained; their rearrangement does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 specifies generation seed 42 for the new language evaluations and reports computational timings as medians over three runs. v1 provides neither practice. Accuracy results still lack numerical uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, while Tables 6–9 add transfer, LoRA, timing, and failure-case outcomes. Examples include MGSM average accuracy of 30.6% versus 33.8% for fine-tuned versus MonoSoup checkpoints, LoRA GSM8K accuracy of 31.92% versus 32.60%, and 83.3-second Qwen3-14B processing. These are newly reported results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix L adds a mathematical argument that a rank-r LoRA update has zero singular values beyond r, limiting MonoSoup's intervention to an at-most-r-dimensional subspace. The original spectral bounds, proofs, coefficient derivation, and Lipschitz analysis remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and central conclusion retain the same claims: alignment motivates data-free, hyperparameter-free spectral editing of a single checkpoint to improve the ID–OOD balance. The added experiments support these retained contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes v1's language difficulty shifts from distributional shifts, adds interpretations about multilingual preservation, and proposes a rank-based limitation explaining attenuated LoRA gains. It removes the conclusion's inconsistent claim that MonoSoup requires a manual variance threshold and adds an explicit boundary excluding adversarial-robustness guarantees.

D1.justification: v2 adds the evaluation-harness version, prompting and decoding settings, checkpoint references, detailed LoRA hyperparameters, hardware, and the sequential layer-wise profiling procedure. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. The original Qwen training description and code/project links are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix L adds focused positioning against LoRA-Pro and PiSSA, distinguishing training-time spectral adaptation from complementary post-hoc editing. References for LoRA, RSLoRA, the evaluation harness, and added benchmarks also appear. The main related-work framing remains stable; publication metadata updates are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the fixed-threshold versus automatic variants, rewrites several experimental and appendix passages, exchanges the ConvNeXt and threshold-ablation appendix order, and adds impact and acknowledgment sections. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–9, moves the 70-checkpoint plot from appendix Figure 12 to main-text Figure 4, and combines the two CKA figures into one four-panel Figure 9. It also redraws plots, revises axes and captions, and reformats the ConvNeXt table, producing substantial display reorganization.

improvement.justification: The new language-shift evaluations address v1's reliance on difficulty-based OOD proxies, while LoRA testing and documented profiling improve assessment of applicability and cost. These benefits are tempered by new reporting errors: Appendix I claims automatic selection matches or exceeds fixed thresholds despite Table 5, and Table 9 displays five pairs while claiming six. Soup-training costs are estimates, which also limits the strength of the efficiency comparison.
